gates.result: SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE = NGS PID TV1051
evidence: NGS archived Puerto Rico shapefile NAME=SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE, PID=TV1051.
Official TV1051 datasheet designation is SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE.
Historical South Base to Morro Lighthouse bearing independently reconciles with TV1051 to TV1029 geometry.
TV1051 DESCRIPTION: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1899 (WCH).
NGS FIRST_RECV=1899; archived-shapefile field semantics define FIRST_RECV as the date first monumented, or first observed for landmarks.

result.location: Low land on the SW side of the harbor; no characteristic neighborhood features.
result.monument: 2-inch iron pipe set vertically in the ground and secured by cement.

reasoning: TV1051 and TV1049 were both described by C&GS in 1899 with initials WCH.
The official 1898-99 C&GS report places W. C. Hodgkins and the BLAKE party in San Juan Harbor in April 1899.
The identification expands initials by independent personnel/field-assignment evidence; the datasheet itself does not spell out Hodgkins's name.

result.shared_monument_type: 2-inch iron pipe set vertically in ground and secured by cement

gates.interpretation: The paired 1899 North Base/South Base designations and matching monument descriptions support a literal San Juan local baseline pair.
gates.limit: A base-measurement field sheet/computation is still required before asserting the measured 1899 base length or measurement method as a primary fact.

gates.result: Recovered GOOD by CGS in 1901; a 20-foot tripod and scaffold signal was erected over TV1051.

gates.limit: This is NGS's superseded Puerto Rico Datum control value; it is not represented as the unreduced raw 1899 field coordinate.

gates.interpretation: Name, chronology and independent Morro bearing geometry all reconcile TV1051 with the historical South Base triangulation station.

source.map_note: Adapted from chart No. 908 U.S. Coast & Geodetic Survey; additions by U.S. Fish Commission, 1899.

gates.result: A diagnostic graticule projection of the NGS Puerto Rico Datum positions for TV1049/TV1051 falls on the mapped low-land southwest side of San Juan Harbor, consistent with the 1899 NGS station descriptions.
limits: The 1899 chart predates formal publication of the Puerto Rico Datum; the projection is contextual, not an independent survey-coordinate validation.
No legible North Base/South Base station labels were found in the 1500-pixel IIIF scan.
Absence of a legible label in this derivative chart does not imply absence of the station from the underlying survey control.

gates.target: Recover a chart/source diagram or higher-resolution control manuscript that explicitly labels SAN JUAN NORTH BASE and/or SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE.

basis: South Base was already monumented in 1899.
SAN JUAN NORTH BASE TV1049 was also monumented in 1899 and described by WCH.
MORRO CASTLE 2 TV1021 was monumented/described in 1900 by C&GS initials SF and later serves as TV1051's primary azimuth mark.
gates.replacement_interpretation: Forney's 1900 Ponce-to-San Juan triangulation is best treated as network integration/reoccupation/extension rather than establishment of South Base.

evidence: TV1021 MORRO CASTLE 2: HISTORY 1900 MONUMENTED CGS; DESCRIBED BY C&GS 1900 (SF).
Official C&GS personnel history records Stehman Forney's Jan-May 1900 triangulation party from Ponce to San Juan.
TV1051 lists MORRO CASTLE 2 as its primary azimuth mark in current NGS control.
gates.limit: The initials SF are expanded to Stehman Forney by contextual corroboration; the TV1021 datasheet itself prints only SF.

gates.target: Recover 1899 base-measurement, angle-observation, computation, reconnaissance or field-record sheets documenting the measured San Juan base and first observation sequence.
Recover any original witness/reference ties beyond the generalized 1899 location description.
